title: Artemis I lifts off (NASA, 16 Nov 2022)
author: NASA / Kennedy Space Center
licence: Public domain (NASA media; no endorsement implied)
attribution: Artemis I Isolated Launch Views, camera 907. NASA/KSC, public domain; trimmed and re-encoded.

scale_hints.object: SLS Block 1 with Orion, full height

expected.meaning: net upward acceleration at liftoff (fitted g is negative: the rocket accelerates up)
expected.source: NASA: 8.8 Mlbf (39.1 MN) liftoff thrust, 5.75 Mlb (2.61 Mkg) liftoff mass; thrust/weight 1.53, so a = 0.53 g = 5.2 m/s²

question: How hard does the rocket accelerate off the pad?
notes: Fixed pad camera at night. The base is below the frame and the lower rocket vanishes into exhaust glare, so the nose (top edge) is the clean point to track. Expected values are approximate: thrust ramps at ignition.

title: Inflatable globe in microgravity aboard the ISS (STEMonstrations: Momentum and Impulse)
author: NASA / ESA astronaut Andreas Mogensen (NASA JSC STEMonstrations)
licence: NASA media: generally public domain (NASA Media Usage Guidelines). The NASA image library entry shows no third-party copyright note in its metadata, but I could not render the images.nasa.gov page itself (JavaScript); the astronaut is ESA, so confirm with NASA guidelines before final release.
attribution: NASA, STEMonstrations: Momentum and Impulse (Andreas Mogensen, ISS), public domain; trimmed and re-encoded.

trimmed_from.note: seconds into the 305 s ~large.mp4 (1920x1080); scaled to 1280x720; audio removed

real_time_evidence: Not documented explicitly; astronaut speech and motion look natural, and this is a normal-speed educational broadcast. Treat as presumed real time.
duplicate_frames: mpdecimate kept 238/240 frames, so essentially no duplicates.

scale_hints.object: astronaut standing height (~1.8 m in microgravity, approx)

expected.source: free flight in orbit, apparent g ~ 0

notes: Wide static shot of the Columbus module. The globe (~0.3-0.4 m, size undocumented) is pushed and caught by the astronaut, so only the free-flight stretches between contacts (first ~2 s, then around 3-4 s) are constant velocity. Ball is ~40-60 px wide. Wider-than-ideal background clutter.
question: Is anything accelerating the globe?
